## 0.11.1 — 2026-11-20
- Switching a note's workspace is now quick, four ways: drag a note from the sidebar onto a workspace in the bar, right-click it and pick "Move to …", press ⌘⇧M (opens ⌘K with the move choices ready), or use the Workspace menu in the note's header. On the phone, open a note and tap a workspace under its title.

## 0.11.0 — 2026-11-20
- Workspaces. Sessions now uses the same workspaces as Notes and Tasks (they arrive through sync, so sign in to see them; Sessions never creates or changes them). A bar above the sidebar switches between All and each workspace, and it filters the note list, Timeline and Browse. A note can belong to one workspace: pick it in the note's header, or press ⌘K and choose "Move this note to …". New notes join the workspace you are looking at.
- The boundary is soft. [[Links]], search and ⌘K still reach every note, notes with no workspace show in all of them (so everything you have today still shows), and "All" shows everything with a small workspace tag. The phone gets the same switcher in Notes.
- Older versions of Sessions don't know about workspaces: if one edits a note, the note can lose its workspace until you set it again.

## 0.10.0 — 2026-11-20
- Quick capture on the Mac. Press ⌘⇧Space (or ⌘K, "Quick capture"), type a thought, press Enter. It goes into the Inbox, or into any note you pick, and the box stays open for the next one. Markers like `[]`, `?` and `>` work as usual.
- Timeline. A new view in the sidebar shows every note on one scrolling line, newest first, grouped by day and month, with Today marked. Each card shows its time, type, people and counts of open tasks, decisions, questions and quotes. Open a card to see the commitments, tasks, decisions, questions, quotes and highlights that came out of it, jump to a topic or person, or open the note. Filter by type or open tasks, or search. It is all read from the note text, so nothing new is stored.

## 0.9.1 — 2026-11-20
- AI helper. In Sync, a new "AI helper" section makes a token that lets an AI helper (like grokbot) read your meeting notes through the sync server: read only, never the Inbox or Scratch. Name it, copy the token once, revoke it any time. It works once the sync server is updated; until then it says the server is too old.

## 0.9.0 — 2026-11-20
- Action bar. Press ⌘K, type, and pick what to do with the open note: pin it, copy it, rename it, change its type, delete it (asks you to press Enter twice), split a card, mark the line your cursor is on as a task, commitment, question, idea, quote and so on, tick it done, highlight the selected words, insert a link, topic or person, move a line or group to the note it links to, bring moved lines back, or jump to a linked note or any other note by name. It also opens the Inbox, Browse, Review, the Quotes tab, a new meeting or braindump, scratch and quiet mode.

## 0.8.0 — 2026-11-20
- Quotes and highlights. Start a line with `>` to mark a quote; end it with `@name` (a dash before it is fine) to credit who said it. Wrap words in `==like this==` to highlight them, or start a line with `=` to highlight the whole line. The right rail gets "Quotes" (with the speaker shown as a byline) and "Highlights" sections, and a section only appears when the note has some. Clicking a speaker opens the new Quotes tab under Browse, which lists every quote and highlight across notes and filters by kind, person and topic.
- On the phone: new `>` and `==` keys in Capture and the editor, quotes and highlights shown inline in a note, and a "Pulled out" list under the text.
- Nothing new is stored. Both are read from the text, so older versions show them as plain lines.

## 0.7.1 — 2026-11-19
- Move a single line that has an inline `[[link]]`. The side panel's new "Move a line" list shows each linked line with a button that moves just that line (and the lines indented under it) to the note it names.
- Moving out of the Inbox is now plain: the lines just show up in the other note, with no trace left in the Inbox and no "moved from" header in the target. This covers group moves and single lines.

## 0.7.0 — 2026-11-19
- Edit notes on the phone. Open a note and tap Edit: change the title and the text, with keys for `[]`, `![]`, `!?`, `?`, `*`, `~`, `#`, `@`, `[[` and indent. It saves as you type and syncs to your Mac. The Notes tab also has "+ Braindump" and "+ Scratch" to start a new one.
- Move a line to any note, during or after capture. In Capture, "Any note…" picks any note as the destination (search included). Tap a captured line, or "Move" on it, to send it to another note, whether your Mac has filed it yet or not. Triage now also lists what is in your Inbox note, and each line can be re-marked, tagged or moved to any note.
- Edits made on two devices at once no longer overwrite each other. When a phone edit and a Mac edit were made from different texts, the newer one is kept and the other becomes a note titled "… (other version)".
